identity: University of Amsterdam ordinary full-time Dutch-taught Religious Studies BA, RIO 50902, 180 EC, academic year 2026–2027. The programme has no formal graduation tracks under adopted OER B1.3; several components are English-taught.
controllingSource: Adopted 2026–2027 programme OER, B1–B5 and Appendix 1; dated ordinary curriculum 39735 and linked course entries provide package membership and progression.
components: The first year also requires a Dutch writing diagnostic. Tutoring and study guidance continue throughout the degree. These requirements carry no credits.
Major Questions in Religious Studies 1: Text Analysis
Major Questions in Religious Studies 2: Lived Religion
This example uses the 24 EC first-year Arabic package. Students choose one package in another discipline; this does not create a separate graduation track.
Attend Arabic 1 before Arabic 2. Pass both courses before starting Arabic 3 and 4.
Attend Arabic 3 before starting Arabic 4. The sequence develops Egyptian Arabic and then Modern Standard Arabic.
Religion, Art and Culture 1: Mythology and Storytelling
Secrets of the West 1: Culture and Counterculture before Modernity

Post-first-year courses require a positive binding study recommendation. The ordinary full-time threshold is 48 first-year EC. Complete Secrets of the West 1 before 2, and both before the research project.
Secrets of the West 2: Culture and Counterculture in the Modern Period
Secrets of the West 3: Culture and Counterculture Research Project
Religion and Spirituality in the Netherlands 1: Concepts and Theories
Religion and Spirituality in the Netherlands 2: Lived Religion
Complete Concepts and Theories before Lived Religion, and both before the Netherlands research project. Students use qualitative methods to investigate contemporary religious practice.
Religion, Art and Culture 2: Sacred Stories in Words and Images
Religion and Spirituality in the Netherlands 3: Research Project
Utopias and Visions of the Future
Bachelor’s Thesis Research Project in Religious Studies

Complete the first year and all compulsory second-year courses before starting. Register for the thesis at the same time. A supervisor must approve the research plan before the first thesis section is written.

Use this 30 EC for electives, a minor, an approved exchange or a placement. Normally no more than 12 EC may be introductory; an approved UvA minor or a same-language sequence can permit up to 24 EC. External study requires Examination Board approval. A placement may occupy up to 12 EC; the Religious Studies and Western Esotericism minors cannot duplicate the compulsory curriculum.
The 12 EC thesis follows the 6 EC research project. Complete the first year and compulsory second-year courses, and pass the research project before the thesis can be assessed.

routeDecision: The previous illustration used Anthropology because it is first in the guide’s package list. Current Debates 1 (59906) requires participation in Introduction to Anthropology, Ethnographies and Academic Writing, and Philosophy of Science; the latter two are absent from that package. The programme OER authorises predetermined 24 EC packages but supplies no waiver for this condition. Reconstructed a valid pathway instead of certifying that choice: Arabic is first in the adopted OER Appendix 1 package list, and the dated guide specifies four 6 EC Arabic courses with a satisfiable sequence. This is a neutral official-order choice independent of UCR content. No formal track is invented, no Anthropology courses are stacked and the unresolved rule for the unselected package is not claimed resolved.
sourceResolution: The public overview omits Anthropology from its written package list and differs on the placement of two second-year units. The adopted OER Appendix 1 and dated catalogue agree on the selected Arabic package and the year-two contents and periods; these control. The generic public grid is not used to override them. The catalogue’s five esotericism/gender courses are optional examples inside the 30 EC group, not an extra compulsory sequence. The 120 EC shortened route, double degrees, honours and part-time timetable are excluded.
definingSubstance: OER B2 identifies historical, comparative, literary and empirical study of religious traditions, heterodox and contemporary religion and spirituality, Western esotericism, changing social roles and Amsterdam as a religious archive/laboratory. The dated first-year traditions and text/lived-religion units establish this base. The upper years deepen myth and sacred images, esoteric cultural history and source research, concepts and fieldwork on Dutch religion, popular culture, utopias and an individual thesis.

progression.yearOne: Six required 6 EC religion units plus Arabic 1–4 at 6 EC each. Arabic 2 follows attendance in 1; pass 1 and 2 before 3 and 4, and attend 3 before 4. The sequence is periods 1, 2, 4 and 5. The diagnostic and recurring tutoring are required 0 EC obligations. Faculty Part A A6.4/A6.6 establishes ordinary full-time positive BSA at 48 first-year EC.
progression.yearTwo: OER B4.4 requires positive BSA for post-propaedeutic courses and delegates additional conditions to the catalogue. Secrets of the West 1, 2 and 3 progress in periods 1, 2 and 3; complete 1 before 2 and both before the research project. Dutch Religion/Spirituality 1–3 progress in periods 4–6, with each required earlier module completed. Philosophy of Science requires 48 first-year EC in History or Religious Studies. Complete year one before year two in this pathway.
progression.yearThree: 12 EC thematic study, 30 EC free choice, 6 EC thesis research project and 12 EC thesis. The thesis and linked research project require the completed first year and all compulsory second-year courses. Register for both together; supervisor approval of the plan precedes the first text. Successful research-project completion is needed before thesis assessment. The selected ordinary periods are project 4 and thesis 5–6.
progression.openSpace: 30 EC remains generic. At most 12 EC level 1 ordinarily, or up to 24 in a recognised UvA minor/same-language sequence under OER B5.1. External study requires Board approval. Minors overlapping compulsory Religious Studies or Western Esotericism units are excluded under B5.2. Placement maximum is 12 EC under B5.3; the guide adds at least 336 hours including the report for 12 EC and programme-coordinator arrangement. No particular host, minor or placement is assumed.
